title: If Statements Practice Exam
description: Assess your skills with if, elif, else, indentation rules, and nested conditionals.

questions.prompt: Which keyword starts a conditional block that runs only when a test is True?
questions.explanation: if evaluates a condition and runs the indented block when it is truthy.

questions.prompt: What is required after an if statement's colon?
questions.explanation: Python uses indentation to define which lines belong to the if block.

questions.prompt: elif is short for 'else if' and checks another condition when previous tests failed.
questions.explanation: elif lets you chain multiple conditions without nesting every branch in else.
85 fails the >= 90 test but passes >= 80, so the elif block runs.

questions.prompt: How many else clauses can a single if statement have?
questions.explanation: else is optional and catches all remaining cases after if/elif tests.

questions.prompt: What happens if you mix tabs and spaces for indentation?
questions.explanation: Python 3 treats inconsistent indentation as an error.

questions.prompt: An empty if block is allowed if you use pass.
questions.explanation: pass is a no-op placeholder so syntactically valid blocks can be empty.
0 is falsy, so the else branch runs.

questions.prompt: Nested if means what?
options: An if block inside another if block
Two if keywords on one line
questions.explanation: Nesting places one conditional inside the body of another.
Both the outer and inner conditions are True, so Enter prints.

questions.prompt: Which condition checks that `name` is not empty?
questions.explanation: Non-empty strings are truthy; empty strings are falsy.

questions.prompt: Only the first matching elif or if branch runs; later branches are skipped.
questions.explanation: Once a condition succeeds, Python skips remaining elif and else for that chain.

questions.prompt:
What is wrong?

if x > 5
    print(x)
questions.explanation: Compound statements like if must end with a colon before the indented suite.
The elif branch matches color == 'red'.

questions.prompt: When is else executed?
options: When all preceding if/elif conditions were False
questions.explanation: else runs as the fallback when no earlier condition matched.
logged_in is False, so the outer else runs before inner checks matter.

questions.prompt: You can write `if 5:` because numbers can be used in boolean context.
questions.explanation: Non-zero numbers are truthy; zero is falsy.

questions.prompt:
Which combines login and age check cleanly?

if logged_in and age >= 18:
options: Runs only when both are True
questions.explanation: and requires both conditions to be truthy.
These are separate if statements; the second runs independently of the first.

questions.prompt: Why indent the body of an if statement?
options: To show which statements belong to the if block
Python has no block syntax without braces
questions.explanation: Indentation defines block structure in Python instead of curly braces.
